### E1-4 Climate-related targets

Evonik supports the objectives of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change and has committed to the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). For the period from 2021 to 2030, we aim to reduce absolute gross Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25 percent. This target is aligned with the SBTi ambition level of “well below 2°C.” The corresponding combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions pathway starts from 6.297 million metric tons of CO₂ equivalents in 2021 and targets 4.723 million metric tons in 2030. Our longer-term trajectory provides for a 100 percent reduction in gross Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2050. At the time of the underlying target disclosure, validation of the targets by SBTi had not yet been completed.

The 2030 target covers a 25 percent reduction in Scope 1 emissions and a 25 percent reduction in market-based Scope 2 emissions relative to the base-year emissions. No percentage reduction target is assigned to location-based Scope 2 emissions. The reported absolute reduction values associated with the target are 600,000 metric tons of CO₂ equivalents for Scope 1 and 200,000 metric tons for market-based Scope 2. The corresponding absolute reduction calculated on a location-based Scope 2 basis is 220,000 metric tons of CO₂ equivalents.

For Scope 3 emissions, Evonik has set a target to reduce emissions by 11.07 percent by 2030. Scope 3 emissions are particularly relevant to Evonik’s upstream value chain, including the raw-material “backpack.” Historically, category 1—purchased chemical raw materials, packaging materials, and indirect goods—has represented more than 40 percent of Scope 3 emissions.

These targets further develop the climate targets adopted by the executive board in February 2019. The previous target was to reduce net Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 50 percent by 2025 compared with 2008. By 2021, a reduction of 43 percent had been achieved, from 9.519 million to 5.468 million metric tons of CO₂ equivalents. The former upstream Scope 3 target, valid through year-end 2021, envisaged a 15 percent reduction compared with 2020.

Greenhouse gas emissions are calculated in CO₂ equivalents in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. A wide range of measures is planned to deliver the targets. In support of emissions reduction, Evonik also aims to reduce both absolute and specific energy consumption by 5 percent between 2020 and 2025.
